method: ENSO fingerprint per grid. ENSO year y = event peaking Nov(y)-Jan(y+1); El Nino if ONI NDJ(y) >= +0.5, La Nina if <= -0.5, otherwise neutral (NOAA ONI). basin_precip: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) PRECTOTCORR at capacity-weighted points near each grid's hydro plants (WRI GPPD), water years 1981/82 onward. Two windows are tested: the Oct-Sep water year and the climatologically wettest 6 months; effect = % difference of mean precipitation in El Nino (La Nina) years vs neutral years; the window with the larger |effect| is kept per phase and the 5,000-shuffle permutation test repeats that choice in every shuffle (corrects for cherry-picking). hydro_generation: Ember monthly hydro TWh per water year, linearly detrended, same composite (low confidence; primary only with >= 10 water years, >= 3 events per phase and >= 4 neutral years). reservoir_level (Zambia, Zimbabwe): G-REALM Kariba level rise from Oct-Nov(y) to Jun-Jul(y+1). Loser in a phase if effect <= -5% with permutation p < 0.1 on the primary variable. Two-sided p-values.

summary.strong_el_nino_note: Exploratory: basin rainfall in the 5 strong El Ninos (1982, 1997, 2009, 2015, 2023) vs neutral years, on the El Nino window; not used for the exposure class.
summary.scope_note: Totals cover the 48 hydro-dependent countries; Sichuan is reported separately (part of China). GW is installed hydro capacity from Ember (latest year; GPPD where Ember has none).
summary.headline: 7 GW of hydropower sits in 4 grids that lose output under El Nino (9 GW in 1 grids lose under La Nina), and extreme El Ninos are projected to come about twice as often.

outlook.summary: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).

cpc.synopsis: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).
cpc.historic_event_text: Chances for a historic event exceeding previous El Niños dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ) are now ~60% for the October-December and November-January periods

geos.note: GEOS-S2S ensemble-mean Nino-3.4 SST anomaly (C), 3-month seasons from the init month

la_nina_after_strong_el_nino.text: Since 1950, 4 of 8 strong El Ninos (ONI NDJ >= 1.5) were followed by La Nina conditions the next winter (ONI NDJ <= -0.5).

projections.text: Extreme El Nino events are projected to roughly double in frequency under greenhouse warming, from about one every 20 years to about one every 10 years (Cai et al. 2014, 20 CMIP models). The increase continues for about a century even after global warming is stabilised at 1.5 C (Wang et al. 2017). Grids that lose hydropower under El Nino therefore face a structural, not only a seasonal, risk.

NOAA PMEL: Frequency of extreme El Ninos to double in the 21st century

enso_years.definition: ONI NDJ(y) >= 0.5 El Nino, <= -0.5 La Nina

context.literature: Ng, Turner & Galelli 2017: more than a third of 1,593 simulated dams show significant annual production anomalies in at least one ENSO phase; effects are strong regionally and partly cancel globally; reservoirs dampen them.
context.both_phases: Both phases matter: El Nino 2023/24 drained Lake Kariba; Brazil's 2021 hydro crisis happened under La Nina.

limitations: Few events: about 15 El Nino and 16 La Nina years since 1981 for rainfall, and only 2-5 per phase in the Ember generation records (mostly 2015/2019 onward). p-values are permutation-based but effect sizes are noisy.

Rainfall is a proxy for hydropower: reservoirs buffer one bad season (Ng et al. 2017 found production anomalies smaller than inflow anomalies), and snowmelt, glaciers and upstream catchments are not captured.
Rainfall is sampled at up to 8 grid points near the largest plants, not over the full upstream catchment (e.g. Namibia's Ruacana is fed from Angola; Tajikistan's Vakhsh from high-mountain snow).
MERRA-2 is a reanalysis: rainfall is a model estimate constrained by observations, not a gauge record.
Non-stationarity: ENSO teleconnections vary between decades and between El Nino flavours (Eastern vs Central Pacific); a historical fingerprint does not guarantee the response of the 2026/27 event.
Neutral-year baseline includes trends (climate change, land use); no detrending is applied to rainfall.
Power-plant locations come from WRI GPPD v1.3 (2021); newer plants are missing.
Kariba level is managed (releases, allocation rules), so it mixes climate and operating decisions.
notes: Southern Brazil (GPPD plants south of 23 S) and Uruguay are computed for validation only; they are not in the 48-country list.
Sichuan rainfall points come from GPPD Chinese hydro plants in a bounding box around the province (lon 97.3-108.6, lat 26.0-34.4).
Ng, Turner & Galelli 2017 (ERL) is the 1,593-dam ENSO-hydropower study; 'more than one third' of dams show significant anomalies in at least one phase.
